Commentary.Commentary: 224 does not look a total which will challenge the tourists. However, if New Zealand can manage to get 2-3 wickets early, we could be in for a thriller. Join us back at 1515 local time (0215 GMT).

England were really good with the ball. Chris Woakes set the tone with a frugal spell first up reading 6-1-13-1. The effect of that was felt by the spinners as Adil Rashid and Moeen Ali combined together to have figures of 4/81 in 20 overs. That broke the backbone of the home side.

Nicholls and Santner batted beautifully, indicating to their top order that had they shown some patience, the Black Caps could have been in a better position. Both made half centuries and were decent enough in finding the gaps for singles and couples, with the occasional boundary.

Colin Munro was dismissed cheaply again, today in the first over. Martin Guptill and Kane Williamson then bided their time, trying to forge a partnership but could not do much. The home side kept losing its wickets to some poor shot selection and the writing looked on the wall at 93/6. But Henry Nicholls and the recent 'Midas' man - Mitchell Santner - added 84 for the 7th wicket to save some blushes for the Kiwis.

A sub-par total from New Zealand. It is a slow pitch, yes, taking some turn, but not so much that it will aid the bowlers to defend a total below 280. The Black Caps struggled for the first hour and then eventually threw their wickets away in frustration.

Absolutely magnificent to watch.

He miscues it up in the air and Alex Hales covers a lot of ground to his right from deep square leg to take the catch. Nasser Hussain on air is impressed with that shot as he reckons that Hales has dropped catches like these in the recent past. End of yet another fantastic innings.

The umpires refer the direct hit upstairs but replays show that Santner is well in.

Should Nicholls have stayed till the end and allowed the in-form Santner to hit hard? Did he go too early? Did he pick the wrong ball? Too many questions when a wicket falls. Nicholls might sit and ponder about those for a while. This stand has given some respect to the Kiwi total.

He is happy with the catch and walks off but the umpires want a second opinion, giving the soft signal as out. Replays confirm that it is a clean catch. The Kiwis are now in a massive hole. Half the side gone.

The ball starts off slowly but once it makes contact with the turf, it zooms towards the long on fence. Mid on gives it a chase but only comes second in the race. First boundary of the match.
Full and straight, watchfully pushed to mid on.
On a length outside off, KW plays at this away from his body and gets a thick outside edge but wide of point. A single to third man. Gets off the mark.
This time he quietly lets the ball go outside off.
On a length outside off, still pretty wide, but inside the guidelines, Kane has a waft again, only to miss.
WIDE. Well outside off, Williamson slashes but cannot reach.
Mark Wood now, to bowl with the second new ball.
Outside off, on a length, Guptill looks to run this down to third man but gets a bottom edge which just misses the stumps. Excellent opening over from Woakes.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone.
Skipper Kane Williamson walks in, in the very first over itself.

OUT! Early strike for England and Munro goes for a duck! Terrific bowling from Woakes. He bangs this in the middle of the pitch and Munro looks to tuck it to the leg side. But the ball gets big on him and the bounce does him in. Takes the leading edge which goes straight up in the air. Both Woakes and the keeper Jos Buttler go for the catch but eventually the glovesman calls for it and takes it. Failure for Munro again.
Full and around middle, Munro comes forward and places it sweetly towards mid off.
Good sharpness from ball 1. Guptill just works this wide of mid on and takes a quick single.
The players are out in the field with play set to begin. Martin Guptill and Colin Munro are the openers for the home side. Chris Woakes will start first up, to Mr. Guptill. Here we go...

Ish Sodhi is giving an interview. He says that he is really enjoying his time playing ODI cricket. Did not feel he would be able to play so much for New Zealand. Admits that he has always looked to pick wickets be it any format and he feels at his best when he is attacking and when the batsmen come at him, which is the norm of today's limited-overs cricket. Adds that in the initial stages of his career, batsmen never used to attack him so much, so he used to target an RPO of around 5. But these days, with batsmen looking to attack him, he believes 6 an over is a decent outing for him. On the previous game, he says that they believed that 400 was on the cards for England but feels nice that it came along nicely for him. Believes that he is a much improved cricketer from what he was a few years ago.

PITCH REPORT - Mark Richardson has a view at the pitch and feels that this looks much better than the one used for the NZ-WIN game. Not quite fluffy but there is some coarse on top. There is grass but evenly spread. Reckons that the pacers will have a say but so will the spinners. The grass feels reasonably thick. There could be some movement in the air as well. The pitch does not feel that rock hard but looks solid. Feels that there could be something for the seamers early on.

New Zealand captain, Kane Williamson, says that he too would have wanted to bowl first. Informs that the surface might do a bit in the first 10 overs but after that, it should be a batting beauty. Informs that ROSS TAYLOR IS NOT PLAYING TODAY and will be replaced by Mark Chapman. On the ground dimensions, Kane admits that fielding and batting plans have to change accordingly to the same. Does not look too much into the past games and says that every match is a new one.

England skipper, Eoin Morgan, says that the pitch looks really good and hence he would prefer chasing. Adds that his team is pretty comfortable knowing what it would like to chase. Informs that there is one forced change - Jason Roy is down with a back spasm, so Alex Hales slots right back in. Admits that every ground in New Zealand is different so accordingly the fielding plans need to change. Agrees that it is a great opportunity to play in a must-win final and along with it, a great chance to prove their worth under pressure.
TOSS TIME! Kane Williamson flips the coin, Heads is the call from Morgan and it is a Head. ENGLAND WILL CHASE.
WEATHER - It had rained last evening but as of now, the skies are pretty clear, without a cloud. The prediction is for no rain and hopefully, it stays that way.

4 matches, 3 thrillers. This has been the story of this NZ-Eng series so far. Both sides will feel they could have wrapped up the series by now, but to be honest, the series status is perfect given the cricket the two teams have played so far. Who will prevail in the decider? Hello and a warm welcome for the fifth and final ODI between New Zealand and England at Hagley Oval, Christchurch.
